threatModel.summary:
Jubarte is an in-process Rust Word-document engine for comparison, inspection, edit plans, tracked-change resolution, Markdown conversion, legacy DOC import, validation, scrubbing and PDF/PNG rendering. Native CLI, PyO3/Python and wasm-bindgen/Node/browser surfaces call the shared engine (src/lib.rs:7-35; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-39; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32). A separately installed Python MCP server brokers document tools over stdio under one directory capability; the Gemini extension starts this server with workspacePath as its root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; gemini-extension.json:5-9). Native CLI self-update is a distinct optional network-and-executable-replacement workflow. Tag releases, local registry publication, CI and external Jules review/remediation are conditional maintainer workflows, not document-runtime capabilities.
Jubarte is a local Rust Word-document toolkit exposed through Rust byte APIs, PyO3 Python, WASM/Node, native and language CLIs, and an optional Python MCP server over stdio. Untrusted DOCX/DOC/Markdown and JSON edit plans feed package admission, XML/legacy parsers, comparisons, edits and PDF/PNG rendering. Native publication and explicit self-update are separate host-authority boundaries (src/lib.rs:7-30,106-174; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-112,373-381). An independent architecture reviewer identified the resource rows below before its execution was interrupted; parent verified their actual consumers offline.
The assigned third validated Standard audit maps the same Rust/native/Python/WASM/Node/MCP engine and ambient font/index resources. Its configuration-to-resource rows are preserved below. Reduction reconciles supplied architecture context only; it adds no source inspection, deployment discovery or validation.
The newly assigned Standard audit confirms the same architecture and adds explicit revision-listing/comparison notes consumers, post-admission HTML multiplicity, and retained WMF text expansion context. Its native/Python/Node/MCP/WASM authority distinctions, conditional deployment assumptions and reported checkout-versus-artifact-name discrepancy are retained. This serial reducer reconciles supplied context only.
Assigned discovery-0004 retains the same architecture and makes Python/npm ambient direct-output and plan-staging authority explicit, adds imported Markdown drawing dependency graphs and the direct public Strict probe, and distinguishes metadata sanitization from structural validity. Serial dedup-0004 reconciles supplied context and evidence only.
Assigned discovery-0005 preserves the same source-backed architecture and distinguishes eager embedded-font alias allocations, UTF-16 XML leak checking, namespace-blind numeric attribute exemptions, relationship-based property discovery and UTF-16 metadata decoding. Serial dedup-0005 reconciles supplied findings/context only; it performs no repository/dependency inspection or independent validation.
assets: Host process availability and bounded memory/CPU while parsing attacker-authored documents (src/admission.rs:42-105; src/legacy_doc.rs:179-216).
Integrity/confidentiality of source documents and generated output; edit snapshot SHA-256 and output alias guards (src/bin/jubarte.rs:1610-1667,1768-1826).

Document text, comments, authors, revisions, embedded media/fonts and retained OPC parts; derived Markdown, JSON snapshots, edit reports, clean/redline DOCX and PDF/PNG can contain the same confidential material (src/lib.rs:17-29; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-217).

Host-process memory/CPU availability. Inspection/edit defaults admit 64 MiB compressed, 64 MiB per part, 256 MiB inflated, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison and rendering use 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB inflated, with the same entry/depth caps (src/admission.rs:63-99; src/inspect.rs:604-620; src/document_comparer.rs:4926-4927; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778).

Filesystem authority granted to MCP: the existing expanded/resolved --root directory, default current directory, held through _OutputRoot. Edit artifacts are root/out_dir/{clean.docx,redline.docx,patch.diff,report.json}, optionally redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png; rendering emits root/out_dir/page-NN.png and optional render.pdf (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:69-108,185-217,234-255,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278).

Ambient native/Python renderer fonts and persistent font index. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides platform user-font locations; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the index, with empty/off disabling it. Defaults resolve to ~/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv on macOS, $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or ~/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Unix, and %APPDATA%/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Windows. The index is beside, not inside, fonts, and saves via a sibling .tsv.<pid>.tmp file (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3090-3107,3182-3229).

Installed native jubarte executable and GitHub release integrity. The updater consumes jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines releases, SHA256SUMS.txt and the platform archive's jubarte binary; RELEASE_KEYS is currently empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so effective authentication is HTTPS plus same-release checksum, not Ed25519 signature verification (src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,198-210,245-257).

Privileged publication resources: GitHub release write token; optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY decoded beneath RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN; local crates.io credentials, npm account/OTP and UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN for PyPI. These have separate provider authority and are used only in release workflows (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-285,297-307,356-369; scripts/release.sh:374-380,919,934-956,1069).

CI runner workspace/cache integrity and external-review credentials. Standard CI runs PR code on self-hosted runners with contents:read and nonpersistent checkout credentials. External Jules review separately receives JULES_API_KEY and a GitHub token with pull-request/check write permissions; companion remediation receives JULES_API_KEY under a trusted-user/event gate (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-46; .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:20-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-54,261-272,320-324).

MCP edit output includes clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff and report.json beneath the selected out_dir: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:195.

Host filesystem contents and existing outputs. MCP grants a directory capability once; CLI publication explicitly grants ambient local access: src/publication.rs:155; src/publication.rs:162; src/publication.rs:175; src/publication.rs:211.

Host memory and CPU handling untrusted packages. Default admission caps compressed bytes at 64 MiB, entries at 10,000, individual inflated parts at 64 MiB, total inflation at 256 MiB and XML depth at 256. Comparison defaults are materially larger: 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB total: src/admission.rs:63; src/admission.rs:87.

Confidential source DOCX, legacy DOC and Markdown content; revision authors, comments, metadata, media, generated agent views, reports, patches, clean documents and redlines (src/lib.rs:15-30; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-217). MCP edit exports have distinct derived destinations under the selected root and out_dir: clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff, report.json, optionally redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png.

Ordinary admission defaults allow 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB inflated total, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison defaults instead allow 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB inflated total (src/admission.rs:63-100).

These are separate capabilities and are not document-processing credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-275,278-307,356-369; scripts/release.sh:919,934-954,1069).

Source-to-edit binding and the integrity of checked primary output. V1 source SHA-256 checking is conditional on the optional plan field; V2 requires source.sha256 equality. Prepared edits retain source, normalized request and actual chosen-primary digests (src/edit.rs:2081-2089, src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-99, src/edit/prepared.rs:157-181).

Process availability and memory during ZIP/XML, legacy document, font, image and rendering work. Agent admission defaults are 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB total inflated, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison defaults are 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB total inflated with the same entry/depth caps. Overrides replace individual values (src/admission.rs:63-99,103-165).

Native font sources and font-index integrity: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR or platform data folders supply fonts; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX or the parent of the font folder supplies font-index.tsv. Cached face paths are read by the renderer and the index is persisted through a sibling temporary file and rename (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3098-3107,3154-3172,3213-3229).

Installed executable authenticity and release publication authority. Current self-update trusts GitHub release delivery plus SHA256SUMS.txt; RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None. CI signing secrets, GitHub contents-write credentials and local package-registry credentials are separate authorities (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:230-264,278-308,356-369; scripts/release.sh:904-919,929-958,1063-1069).

Confidential document bytes, revisions/comments/authors and derived renderings/reports; integrity of selected input/output files and admitted package structures (src/lib.rs:17-30; src/publication.rs:146-225).
MCP root filesystem capability; native executable integrity on self-update; release publishing/signing authority (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-275,356-369; src/update.rs:25-48,198-258).

Native renderers read installed/user/Word cloud-cache fonts and persist a per-user font index, distinct from document output-root authority (src/convert/font.rs:2228-2236,2633-2652,3090-3107,3213-3227).

MCP edit outputs are root/out_dir/{clean.docx,redline.docx,patch.diff,report.json}, optional redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png, available to authorized root filesystem readers and reported to attached client; native OutputRoot publishes with default no overwrite and per-file atomicity (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:153-217; src/publication.rs:168-199).
trustBoundaries: Document author -> Rust parsing/rendering -> caller process. admission bounds compressed bytes, entry counts, per-part/total inflation and selected XML depth/tag policy; downstream XML, numeric layout, images/fonts and legacy fields require their own effective controls (src/admission.rs:442-580,788-827; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798).

Python/Node/native CLI callers choose ambient local input/output paths; these callers already possess operator file authority. MCP clients instead provide relative document/output names beneath --root, default current working directory; build_server resolves that root once and _OutputRoot retains native cap_std::Dir authority for actual I/O (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-112,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1279; src/publication.rs:146-200).

MCP/native rendering -> ambient font resources: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides the platform user font directory; macOS ~/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Unix $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or ~/.local/share/jubarte/fonts, Windows %APPDATA%/jubarte/fonts. Fonts are read by conversion outside the document root (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652).

Rendering -> persistent font index: JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX selects a path; empty/off disables it; default parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv. FONT_INDEX loads that path and save merges and writes path.with_extension(tsv.<pid>.tmp), then renames it to the index (src/convert/font.rs:3100-3107,3213-3229). This is component ambient authority, distinct from tool document/output confinement.

Explicit self-update -> fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines GitHub release and SHA256SUMS.txt -> extracted platform executable -> installed binary. TLS/checksum verification, optional compiled version-gated signing policy, and lstat regular-file hook enforce distinct steps (src/update.rs:25-48,198-257,274-285,299-321; Cargo.toml:137-148).

Privileged release workflows: release.yml optionally signs with secret-store ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, computes SHA256SUMS.txt and publishes GitHub assets. Operator scripts/release.sh:976-1012 can recover workflow artifacts into dist/release, compute checksums and create a release without that signing step.

Caller-supplied DOCX/ZIP/XML/media/fonts cross into the host engine. Admission counts actual inflation, checks package identity, names and XML limits; production archive opening rejects header/extent/special-entry defects. Low-level permissive parse_xdocument does not apply input policy: callers of raw XML APIs must select checked parsing or prevalidate. The deliberate debug archive reader is an inspection exception (src/admission.rs:13-28,439-566; src/opc/archive.rs:20-51; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:21-36,98-135; SECURITY.md:132-139).

Legacy DOC is a separate OLE/FIB/piece-table parser, not a ZIP-admission path. It converts the supported main story to Markdown/DOCX and explicitly excludes encrypted/obfuscated and older Word formats (src/legacy_doc.rs:13-50).

Edit-plan author transfers requested mutations and optionally source identity to the engine. Schema version and a supplied source_sha256 are checked; the v1 source guard is optional, not an authorization or mandatory freshness credential (src/edit.rs:97-106,2072-2094). Filesystem publication is a separate boundary from in-memory edit acceptance.

Native CLI uses ambient caller-selected output paths. publish_paths holds each parent directory, stages into parent/.jubarte-<uuid>.partial/bytes, uses Unix staging mode 0700, and commits per file; OutputRoot additionally validates portable relative names and confines capability-relative I/O. Multi-file publication is explicitly not atomic across the set, and errors record already committed files (src/publication.rs:83-143,146-225,228-273,420-505). Python and npm general-output helpers instead directly call Path.write_bytes/fs.writeFileSync; native publication controls cannot be assumed for those helpers (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-113,126-132; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-79,106-110).

MCP caller gains document read/write operations only within the operator-selected root. Python resolve-based checks are early diagnostics; native cap-std OutputRoot owns the actual read/write confinement. overwrite is caller-controlled, false by default; annotations are hints, not per-tool authorization. stdio possession is the transport access boundary; no distinct users/tenants are established by this adapter (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,152-160,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-199).

Native Markdown image references cross from document content into local reads. Effective resource root is --resource-path or the Markdown file's parent, falling back to current directory. Percent-decoded targets must canonically remain under that root and actual reads use its held OutputRoot capability; URL schemes are refused. The library's image callback is separately supplied by the embedding caller, while Python/npm CLI reject resource_path support (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2870,2936-2943,3365-3400; src/markdown/mod.rs:196-198; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1057-1064; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727).

Native/Python rendering may read installed fonts and update the ambient per-user/configured index even when invoked through MCP. MCP's document-path capability is not a whole-process filesystem sandbox. Browser/WASM uses embedded/bundled faces rather than installed fonts; its byte APIs do not expose native OutputRoot publication (src/convert/font.rs:2258-2285,2633-2652,3095-3107,3182-3229; README.md:901-920; Cargo.toml:149-152).

Self-update crosses from GitHub release service/assets into executable replacement. Noninteractive operation requires --check or --yes; a terminal otherwise confirms replacement. Default selection installs newer versions; explicit --version permits downgrade. Unix archive member is jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte, Windows member ends jubarte.exe; an extracted regular-file verification hook runs before the delegated swap. Current release keys are empty, so signature support is compiled but not enforcing (src/update.rs:91-124,144-160,186-257,307-320).

Tag-triggered release builders have contents:read; the separate release job has contents:write. Archives/wheels are downloaded into dist, optional signing rewrites archives before SHA256SUMS.txt generation, then gh publishes dist/* to the tag. The signing private key is step-scoped and decoded into a temporary directory removed by EXIT trap (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-89,230-285,297-307,317-322,356-369).

Local scripts/release.sh uses the operator's separate registry credentials, validates tool/auth availability, verifies the tagged engine stamp and prompts for the exact version unless YES bypass applies. It also executes an external app checkout's scripts/release-engine.sh selected by JUBARTE_APP_DIR or jubarte-app; that external implementation and its downstream authority are absent from this repository (scripts/release.sh:374-389,870-899,919,934-956,1069).

Ordinary PR CI crosses into self-hosted execution with contents:read and persist-credentials:false; those settings govern GitHub-token persistence/permissions, not runner filesystem isolation. Jules review and companion remediation are independent grants: reviewer action receives PR/check-write GitHub token and Jules key, with enable_approve:false; remediation permits only configured trusted author/dispatcher/event combinations, then requests AUTO_CREATE_PR with require_plan_approval:false and starting_branch equal to mutable PR head_ref. Untrusted document suppliers cross into in-process ZIP/XML/media parsing. Direct unchecked archive opening is retained for diagnostic inspection: src/admission.rs:439; src/admission.rs:531; src/opc/archive.rs:20; src/opc/archive.rs:42.

Public checked XML parsing validates before DOM construction; permissive parse_xdocument remains a different API whose caller must establish appropriate trust/admission. Tag defaults include 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte qualified attribute names, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:49; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:119; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:134.

MCP caller arguments cross into host document reads and publication. Python resolves paths for early diagnostics, while native _OutputRoot performs capability-relative read/publish using the directory held by publication::OutputRoot. Tool annotations are hints to the host, not an approval or per-tool authorization mechanism: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:72; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:84; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:101; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1254; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1260; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1265; docs/adoption/mcp.md:39.

Native CLI operators select ambient input/output paths. src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273 invokes publication::publish_paths, whose root=None backend opens output parents with ambient authority (src/publication.rs:203-225,431-446). Outputs stage beside their destination in .jubarte-<UUID>.partial/bytes, with Unix staging directory mode 0700 and exclusive creation (src/publication.rs:472-505). Publication stages all files first but commits per file; failures can leave named committed outputs, and Windows directory synchronization is intentionally a no-op (src/publication.rs:100-130,168-174,387-405). This is not an all-files transaction.

Python and Node CLI callers retain ambient local filesystem authority. Python's _read_side consumes caller paths and _write calls Path.write_bytes; Node's read and write helpers call fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73-83,126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-56,106-111). Native staged-publication properties cannot be assumed for these helpers.

The MCP operator grants a directory root once; a connected stdio client can invoke all registered read/write tools within that grant. --root defaults to current working directory, is expanded/resolved, and must be a directory; no HTTP listener or application authentication is configured in this entrypoint (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381). Python containment checks are early diagnostics; actual reads and publications use _native._OutputRoot, backed by cap_std directory authority and portable relative-write validation (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:69-108; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:153-199,228-273,431-463). overwrite is a per-call replacement capability, defaulting false. ToolAnnotations are metadata, not a separate authorization layer (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,153-160).

CLI Markdown image targets cross into local filesystem reads only through a selected resource root: explicit --resource-path wins, otherwise the Markdown file's parent, otherwise '.' (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2937-2943). The loader canonicalizes and holds that directory capability, applies image policy and reads relative to the capability; URLs are not fetched by this loader (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2877). This capability is separate from output publication authority.

Native renderer font discovery is ambient OS-account access, independent of MCP's document/output root. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides per-user locations; absent it, Windows uses APPDATA/jubarte/fonts, macOS HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, and other native platforms XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652). Native discovery also examines named system/Word font directories and HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; the document-supplied family must be a single normal path component for that derived cloud directory (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2281-2309).

Browser/Node WASM callers pass byte arrays and JSON options into the engine. The bindings disable default engine features, omit native publication on wasm32 and support comparison-budget overrides; the binding explicitly warns that its 2 GiB inflated default can exceed practical WASM heap capacity (jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-23; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:63-97). Hosting applications own admission tuning, upload authorization, origin policy, worker isolation and persistence.

Explicit jubarte self-update crosses from GitHub release metadata/assets into executable replacement. Repo is jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines; the chosen archive member is jubarte-<version>-<platform>/jubarte[.exe]; SHA256SUMS.txt is configured; extracted binary must lstat as a regular file (src/update.rs:25-27,91-109,198-210,299-321). Without --check/--yes, noninteractive runs stop before lookup; installation requires confirmation unless --yes; explicitly selected versions may downgrade (src/update.rs:120-125,144-160,234-247). Current RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean signature enforcement is inactive (src/update.rs:44-48,274-285).

Tag-driven GitHub release automation builds platform archives/wheels with read-only job permissions, then a separate contents:write job signs when configured, computes checksums and publishes dist/* to the triggering tag's release (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-89,230-275,295-321,356-369). The signing secret is scoped to the signing step, decoded into RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and removed by an EXIT trap; the signing tool and runner are recipients of this authority (.github/workflows/release.yml:261-307).

The local release script separately publishes the Rust package, both npm packages and PyPI artifacts. Typed version confirmation precedes pushing unless YES is set, then each registry operation uses its own tool/account authority (scripts/release.sh:877-919,929-959,1063-1069). The script calls a downstream app checkout, but that application's implementation is absent from this repository and is not included as inspected architecture (scripts/release.sh:141-175).

PR automation crosses repository-controlled PR source, descriptions and tool output into external actions and agent sessions. The normal review workflow excludes fork/Dependabot PRs and grants contents:read, pull-requests:write and checks:write; companion remediation additionally gates session creation on TRUSTED_USERS=['arthrod'] and selected events, uses AUTO_CREATE_PR and require_plan_approval=false (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-52,259-272,320-324). External action internals, Jules integration permissions and runtime restrictions are not present here.

CI/docs workflows execute checked-out repository code on self-hosted runners for pull_request events. Workflow token permissions are contents:read and checkout disables persisted credentials, but host filesystem, network, persistent-state isolation and runner admission controls are external deployment controls (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-40,72-99; .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-86,98-99).

Validated audit refinements: package admission's extension-based selection does not cover relationship-resolved notes with non-XML suffixes (src/admission.rs:533-570; src/document_comparer.rs:6318-6328,6461-6479). Admission also ignores DTD while the raw DOM disagrees on declaration boundaries (src/admission.rs:798-820; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:539-547,660-662). These are findings, not assertions that the intended policy is fully enforced.

Untrusted DOCX/ZIP/XML bytes cross into package admission and then DOM/document operations. Opened::open admits using default limits, normalizes Strict packages and opens/parses within those limits. General rendering calls admit_package before package/DOM construction. The common archive opener rejects reported structural defects, while the deliberately unchecked opener supports triage and admission's own typed checks (src/inspect.rs:604-622; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51).

Raw XML library callers choose between checked and permissive APIs. try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates before constructing the DOM; parse_xdocument explicitly requires a prior gate and does not enforce input policy itself. Shared defaults include 1,024 element attributes, 1,024 attribute-name bytes, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:25-36,48-57,91-98,119-135).

Edit requests cross from caller-authored plans to document mutations. V1 checks a supplied source hash, refuses blank authors and signed/macro-bearing inputs; V2 requires the exact source hash and resolves scope/context before operations. These are document-consistency controls, not user authentication or authorization (src/edit.rs:2072-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-110). Dry run and application share in-memory preparation; filesystem publication remains a separate host operation (src/edit/prepared.rs:5-13,157-186).

Native CLI users grant ambient authority through selected input/output paths. publish_paths opens and retains each actual parent rather than enforcing a global document root; staging uses an exclusive UUID directory and file, with Unix staging directory mode 0700. Publication is atomic per file and records partial commits/durability uncertainty rather than promising set-wide rollback (src/publication.rs:5-7,83-143,203-225,420-505).

The MCP connected client can invoke registered read and write tools within the root chosen by the server operator. Startup defaults --root to cwd, resolves it once and serves stdio. Python containment checks are preliminary diagnostics; actual document reads and output publication pass through native _OutputRoot and cap-std directory-relative operations. No per-tool user identity or tenant separation is established; tool annotations are hints, while OutputRoot owns filesystem confinement (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276; src/publication.rs:146-199).

Native font discovery/cache is a separate authority from document-root publication. Font-family lookup can inspect system, Word, cloud and configured user-font directories; cloud family names must be one normal path component. The index may read cached face paths and write its configured file outside the MCP root. Its enforcing boundary is host environment/filesystem authority, not OutputRoot (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2263-2315,2633-2652,2855-2862,3098-3107,3154-3172,3213-3229).

WASM byte APIs do not receive native publication::OutputRoot because that module is compiled only outside wasm32. Python and WASM bindings disable engine default features and request only cli grammar, so optional self-update is not part of those engine dependencies. Node's separately shipped CLI grants ambient filesystem access through node:fs around the WASM engine; its read/write helpers are distinct from native staged publication (src/lib.rs:147-149,163-165; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-39; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-23; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-79,106-111).

Self-update is an explicit native CLI capability. It selects fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines repository, platform archive and inner binary path; requests checksum verification and regular-file verification; prompts unless --yes, and --check does not install. Current keys leave signature verification disabled. Dependency-owned download, archive extraction and executable-swap behavior is not established merely by this wrapper (src/bin/jubarte.rs:3892-3896,4062-4073; src/update.rs:25-48,186-257,274-285,299-321).

Release publication is privileged operator/CI work, separate from document processing. CI triggers on v* tags, checks tag/package version, grants build jobs contents:read and release job contents:write, optionally signs assets with step-scoped ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, then publishes dist/* using step-scoped GH_TOKEN. Local release script has packaging dry runs and version confirmation unless YES, then separately publishes crates.io, two npm packages and PyPI with configured credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,31-49,230-264,278-308,317-322,356-369; scripts/release.sh:729-747,874-888,904-919,929-958,1039-1069).

Untrusted DOCX/ZIP/XML, legacy DOC, embedded images/fonts and edit plans enter the engine. Default admission bounds archive/part bytes 64 MiB, 10000 entries, inflation 256 MiB, XML depth 256; comparison allows 512 MiB archive/part and 2 GiB inflation. Permissive parse_xdocument requires a prior gate (src/admission.rs:15-28,63-99; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:21-36).

MCP stdio client invokes document tools under operator --root (default cwd). Python resolves paths for diagnostics; native _OutputRoot owns confined reads/publication through a held capability. Annotations are hints, not caller authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1277; src/publication.rs:146-199).

Native CLI grants ambient paths with staged per-file publication. Python/Node CLI ambient reads/writes are separate from MCP confinement (src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:203-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:142-145; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-132; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-56,106-110).

Native Markdown images use --resource-path or Markdown parent directory; URL schemes/canonical escape targets are refused, followed by capability-relative read (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2876,2936-2943).

Self-update enters executable replacement only on explicit command and confirmation/--yes. RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean checksum-only today; optional Ed25519 support is inactive (src/update.rs:25-48,120-125,198-258,274-285; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82).

Tag-triggered release builds are read-only; release job has contents:write, signing step receives signing secret and publishes dist/* with workflow token. These are CI/maintainer authorities (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-55,230-275,356-369).

Native rendering, including MCP rendering, has separate ambient font discovery/cache I/O: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides user font roots; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX controls index persistence independently of document-root grants (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3098-3107,3192-3229).

PR workflows run checked-out code on self-hosted runners sharing the private mbx cache http://mbx-cache:7543, namespace jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines. Comments promise protected-push publishing and PR reads, but server writer authorization and object validation are absent from this repository (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-17,34-48,72-101; .github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-22).

Outgoing privacy certification has independent controls: the leaks XML decoder must honor supported UTF-16, matching business XML attributes must not inherit namespace-blind numeric exemptions, metadata discovery must follow actual property targets, and Part::load must consistently decode selected property XML. A fix to one does not subsume the others (src/scrub.rs:188-199,357-385,467-475,484-490,522-552; src/opc/mod.rs:560-564).

Eager embedded-font loading copies and retains each unknown alias/style even when runs do not use it. Resource accounting must distinguish stored bytes from decoded buffers and alias multiplicity; Arc container values do not imply resolved-part sharing (src/convert/mod.rs:806-809; src/convert/font_table.rs:177-193,205-231).
attackerCapabilities: An attacker can author DOCX ZIP entries, relationship targets/types, XML structures and numeric attributes, embedded media/font bytes, legacy DOC character streams, Markdown and edit-plan values that a caller elects to process.

An MCP client can invoke registered tools over its existing stdio connection and request reads/writes within the granted root; overwrite=true explicitly permits replacement there. No remote listener or tenant model is established by the source (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:93-112,373-381).

Document control does not imply control of host environment variables, font directories/index, release assets, signing credentials, operator checkout or trusted MCP root. No new authority is inferred from already possessing those privileges.

A document supplier can control DOCX/ZIP/XML, embedded media/fonts, legacy DOC bytes and Markdown; it need not control host accounts or filesystem configuration. Denial-of-service and unintended host access boundaries are relevant for library callers even without a demonstrated public deployment.

An MCP client can invoke exposed document tools and choose relative paths, plans and overwrite within the operator-granted root. It does not thereby possess arbitrary host-path, network, release or registry authority. Directory contents visible to other MCP clients are not isolated per caller by this adapter (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-160).

A same-repository PR contributor can control reviewed source/diff and PR metadata and cause applicable CI/review workflows. Fork PR eligibility, GitHub workflow approval settings and self-hosted runner registration determine additional reachability; no assumption of repository-secret or runner-administrator control is needed or granted by this model.

A release-asset adversary would need authority over published release artifacts, beyond normal document input. Current checksum-only update trust means archive and matching checksum share the release service's authority; documentation acknowledges this limitation. Signing keys, registry credentials and repository-write tokens are separate capabilities (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:44-48).

External Jules actions receive explicitly configured credentials and repository context, but their internal authorization, remote session permissions and enforcement cannot be established from this repository's workflow declarations alone.

A document supplier can control input package structures, XML, media, embedded fonts and document content without already controlling the host filesystem, operator environment or release infrastructure: src/admission.rs:439; src/opc/archive.rs:42; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:134.

An MCP client can supply tool arguments, document paths, edit plans, output directories and explicit overwrite flags within the granted root; it does not thereby receive ambient CLI authority. The server is started on stdio, without a network listener: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:152; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:381.

An actor able to replace release archives and their adjacent checksum file has meaningful influence over checksum-only updater installations. Such release-write authority is a separate prerequisite, not an ordinary document supplier capability: src/update.rs:44; src/update.rs:48; src/update.rs:245; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59.

The assigned validated findings additionally distinguish a less-trusted local writer of a plan/index staging parent from a document supplier. A symlink overwrite requires a separate writable shared parent, predictable/observable process PID and victim-writable referent; ordinary document control does not grant those prerequisites.

A document supplier can control document bytes, ZIP/XML structure, relationships, embedded media/fonts, Markdown content and document metadata that callers choose to process. This does not grant control of trusted environment variables, arbitrary operator-selected paths, release credentials or executable installation decisions.

A connected MCP client can choose tool arguments, source files and output destinations inside the operator-granted root and request overwrite=true. These are existing tool capabilities; new security impact would require exceeding the root grant, unintended disclosure to another actor, bypassing promised replacement restrictions or attacking the host process.

A library/WASM caller can choose API input bytes and exposed options, including input-limit overrides. A hosted service may expose a narrower subset, but no such service deployment or tenant model is established by this repository.

A PR contributor can control PR source/text subject to repository contribution permissions and workflow event gates. Same-repository authorship, trusted-user session gates, self-hosted runner admission and external agent authority must be evaluated separately; fork authors are not automatically authorized for secret-bearing Jules workflows.

Release-asset modification or privileged tag/release control is a distinct prerequisite for updater supply-chain impact. Ordinary document control does not confer it; checksums fetched with release assets do not independently authenticate the publisher (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80).

A document supplier controls package names, relationships, XML, revision/comment content, embedded fonts/images and document complexity submitted to a consumer. This does not imply host configuration, MCP root directory, registry accounts or release asset access (src/admission.rs:13-28; SECURITY.md:36-78).

A connected MCP client can request supported reads/mutations under operator-selected root and overwrite=true. Tools expose that shared root capability, not a separate tenant identity. Escape would add host access not granted (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-168,258-277,373-381).

An edit-plan author controls operations and V1 source-hash inclusion. Author strings and revision metadata are document data rather than authenticated identities. Consistency guards are not authorization (src/edit.rs:2081-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-110).

A malicious local peer may possess filesystem access to writable output/cache directories depending on deployment; this is conditional, not assumed. Native held handles, exclusive staging and MCP path validation are relevant to races when such a peer exists (src/publication.rs:146-148,228-270,420-505).

Control of GitHub release assets, signing material or registry accounts is a conditional supply-chain starting capability, not ordinary document input. Current checksum-only update authenticity depends on release authority and transport/dependency controls; distinct signing-key compromise is not required because trusted keys are empty (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82).

Document suppliers control package/XML/relationship/font/image/Markdown bytes, not operator environment, MCP root grants or release infrastructure (src/admission.rs:15-28; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2876).

Authorized MCP clients read/publish inside granted root including explicit overwrite; tools do not grant updater or ambient path authority (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,153-217,373-381).

Control of release assets permits changing archive and adjacent checksum; this is a separate supply-chain starting capability not authenticated by checksum-only policy (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-77; src/update.rs:44-48,245-248).
securityObjectives: Reject malformed or excessive document input before unbounded recursion, scalar-driven allocation or algorithmic amplification reaches the host process.
Keep document relationship resolution within in-memory package data and do not fetch external references (src/convert/mod.rs:21310-21319; src/admission.rs:14-23).
Enforce held-root filesystem confinement and no-clobber publication; retain source identity for guarded native edits (src/publication.rs:419-574; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1610-1667,1768-1826).
Install only checksum-verified release binaries and enforce configured signing keys/version rules and regular-file validation; never expose CI secret material in generated analysis.

Refuse unsafe or resource-policy-violating untrusted packages before unbounded package/DOM work, while preserving explicit caller obligations for permissive low-level APIs and process-level CPU/memory limits (src/admission.rs:13-28,63-99; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:21-36; SECURITY.md:69-75).

Keep document relationships from becoming unintended network/filesystem authority; preserve separate explicit image-loader and native font-resource policies (src/admission.rs:20-22; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2870; src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652).

Keep MCP document reads/writes beneath the held directory capability, refuse unsafe portable output names and default to preserving existing outputs; distinguish per-file atomicity from multi-output transaction success (src/publication.rs:146-199,228-273; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:91-108).

Bind supplied edit snapshots to actual source bytes, accurately report refusal/partial publication, and keep author labels and SHA content keys distinct from user authentication (src/edit.rs:2081-2089; src/publication.rs:89-98,123-130; SECURITY.md:77-86).

Only explicitly requested native self-update may replace the executable; enforce configured checksum/signature policy and regular-file extraction verification without presenting current checksum-only operation as signed-release authentication (src/update.rs:120-124,234-257,307-320).

findings.summary: An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. severity.changeConditions: Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

rootCause.summary:

findings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
findings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. findings.title: Shallow malformed XML can bypass admission and overflow the DOM parser stack
findings.summary:
A DOCX main part containing many sibling `

` tags passes the tolerant admission depth check as shallow empty elements. The DOM parser consumes the two slashes as attribute quotes and treats those siblings as nested open elements, enabling stack exhaustion despite the configured XML depth limit.

severity.rationale: A small attacker-authored document can cause unbounded parser recursion in the host process through a public parser boundary. Impact is availability loss; shared service use and process isolation determine wider impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent source review confirmed both product parser paths and cached quick-xml 0.42.0 tokenization: final /> is stripped into an Empty event and HTML attributes accept the remaining unquoted slash.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled recursion caused by parser disagreement

codeEvidence.explanation: Package admission explicitly enables html_attributes.

codeEvidence.explanation: Tag policy selects quick-xml HTML attribute tokenization.

codeEvidence.explanation: After both slashes are consumed as pseudo-quotes the empty-element check sees > and treats the tag as open.

codeEvidence.label: render dom
codeEvidence.explanation: Admitted main XML reaches this DOM parser in the public rendering path.

rootCause.summary:
The admission gate allows HTML-style unquoted attributes, while the downstream parser assumes any first character after `=` opens a quoted value. For `

` admission sees an empty tag with an unquoted slash value. DOM parsing consumes both slashes as delimiters, sees an ordinary closing `>` and recursively nests following siblings. Thus reader depth is not the depth of the representation actually constructed.

findings.remediation: Make tolerant attribute tokenization identical between admission and DOM construction or refuse unsupported unquoted values, and enforce a real construction-depth limit or use an iterative DOM parser.

counterEvidence: Admission checks matching end tags, XML depth and tag budgets; these checks apply to quick-xml's different interpretation.
The strict checked XML API rejects unquoted attributes, but package admission deliberately uses the tolerant mode.
limitations: No adversarial application input was executed.

The shared chicago_label formatter repeats a UTF-8 symbol roughly n/4 times without a length bound, allowing gigabyte allocations during list rendering, ordinary section-page processing and Markdown numbered-list views.

severity.rationale: Attacker-selected document numbers directly cause excessive allocations in public document-processing paths. Impact is host-process availability; no remote service is assumed and memory isolation limits wider damage.
severity.changeConditions: Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Independent source tracing confirms unbounded document-selected u32 starts, dispatch to `chicago_label()` and its direct `str::repeat()` expansion, plus the Markdown sibling caller.

rootCause.summary: List starts/startOverrides and section pgNumType starts retain full u32 values. Numbering::next_marker uses the authored first counter and substitutes format_num output; section_page_label independently dispatches its page counter through format_num. Chicago calls chicago_label, which computes i=n.saturating_sub(1) and MARKS[i%4].repeat(i/4+1) without a bound. Markdown list-label generation uses the same shared formatter. Counter saturation prevents overflow but retains enormous values; ordinary paragraph processing evaluates chapter/page labels even before an empty bookmarks loop.

findings.remediation: Bound generated byte/glyph length inside the shared Chicago formatter before repetition, with a documented safe cycle/fallback or typed refusal. Apply that bound to all list, startOverride, section-page and Markdown/direct list_number callers; do not rely on input bytes, counter saturation or later clipping.

counterEvidence: Other alphabetic and Roman formats have explicit wrapping maxima, but Chicago has no corresponding bound (convert/mod.rs:6492-6520).
Admission constrains input bytes and depth; it does not constrain generated label length.
Counter saturation prevents integer overflow but preserves enormous values.

Admission restricts input bytes and XML structure, not the expanded label. Sibling alphabetic and Roman formatters explicitly cycle at ALPHA_LABEL_MAX and ROMAN_LABEL_MAX (lines 6491-6514); Chicago lacks an equivalent bound.
Host process resource limits can contain failure but do not bound the allocation request.
limitations: No allocation-triggering input or runtime rendering was executed.
No application code, generated input or runtime reproduction was executed.
validation.method: Previously validated independent offline source traces; semantic reduction only
validation.summary: The validated traces establish full-u32 list/startOverride propagation and independent section-page and Markdown numbered-list callers. A level with chicago, lvlText %1 and start 4294967295 yields 1073741824 repetitions of a three-byte symbol, requesting 3 GiB before shaping/copying. Section labels are evaluated on ordinary paragraphs even without bookmarks. Alphabetic/Roman siblings cycle at explicit maxima; Chicago does not. Source XML remains small and shallow.

dataflow.summary: List w:start/startOverride -> Numbering::next_marker -> placeholder render -> format_num(Chicago,n); section pgNumType -> section_page_label -> format_num; Markdown numbered-list counters -> list_number -> shared Chicago formatter -> str::repeat.

impact.rationale: Memory exhaustion and host-process availability loss.
impact.why: An admitted start value of 4294967295 causes chicago_label to repeat a three-byte symbol 1073741824 times, requesting roughly 3 GiB for one label before downstream shaping/copying. The section-page route evaluates the label for ordinary paragraph blocks even without bookmarks.

likelihood.rationale: Tiny decimal values amplify directly into very large allocations without configuration changes.
likelihood.why: The numeric input is document-controlled and reaches the sink with default conversion.

limitations: No data disclosure or code execution established; remote service exposure is deployment-dependent.

reachability.summary: An untrusted DOCX author controls numbering format and counters. A victim needs only to render or generate a Markdown numbered-list label view; the section-page route needs no bookmarks, special option or privileged setting.
reachability.entrypoint: Public PDF/PNG/render APIs, Markdown numbered-list label views and shared list_number callers

attackPath.summary: Request a numbered-list view or rendering of a DOCX with a Chicago list start/startOverride or section pgNumType start near u32::MAX.

remediationTests: Cover maximum u32 Chicago start and startOverride values without large allocations.
Exercise section page labels and Markdown list-label views as well as ordinary list rendering.
Reject or safely cycle a Chicago list start/startOverride at u32::MAX.
Exercise Chicago section pgNumType start=u32::MAX on an ordinary paragraph and direct list_number callers.
preventiveControls: Bound derived dimensions and generated output independently from archive/XML input byte limits.

findings.title: Rendering an HTML chunk can allocate gigabytes from a single colspan value
findings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory.

severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.
severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Both independent baseline and focused investigator identified the mechanism; parent verified input parsing, post-admission expansion and allocation loop statically. No runtime reproduction was executed.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.

findings.remediation: Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/aggregate column counts before generating any table XML. Charge all HTML/MHT-generated WML, including repeated/nested tables, to a cumulative byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion and return a typed input-limit refusal before allocation or DOM construction.

finding.title: Converting an HTML altChunk can allocate billions of table columns
finding.summary: A small DOCX containing an HTML altChunk with a huge numeric `colspan` can exhaust memory or CPU during conversion. The importer accepts the value as `usize` and generates one `<w:gridCol>` per column before any layout or raster limit applies.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can trigger excessive allocation through the public conversion API with a small input and no configuration changes. Availability of the host process or WASM instance is affected; no remote service deployment, code execution or data theft is established. External process limits constrain collateral impact.
severity.changeConditions: A shared upload-processing process increases impact; bounded table columns and a checked expansion budget remove the amplification.

confidence.rationale: Parent source review confirms direct numeric parsing, table-close dispatch, unbounded output loop, and public conversion reachability; no application execution.

taxonomy.category: Unbounded allocation from HTML numeric input

codeEvidence.label: conversion public
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller-provided DOCX bytes enter public PDF conversion and reach with_pages/with_layout.

codeEvidence.label: conversion layout
codeEvidence.explanation: Admission happens before HTML expansion; the referenced chunk bytes are sent to altchunk::expand and resulting XML goes straight to a DOM.

codeEvidence.label: chunk repeat
codeEvidence.explanation: Each altChunk reference is loaded, decoded to HTML and converted by html_to_wml.

codeEvidence.label: html parser
codeEvidence.explanation: The HTML tokenizer dispatches each td/th opening tag to Builder::start and table closes to end_table.

codeEvidence.label: span input
codeEvidence.explanation: The colspan string is parsed into an unrestricted usize and retained on the cell stack.

codeEvidence.label: span count
codeEvidence.explanation: end_table sums cell spans into the table's column count without a cap.

codeEvidence.label: span output
codeEvidence.explanation: The column count controls one allocated XML grid-column string per iteration.

rootCause.summary: `Builder::start` treats `colspan` as any positive usize. `end_cell` retains that span, and `end_table` sums it into `cols` before a `0..cols` loop materializes XML for every column. Package admission runs on the original DOCX and does not bound this derived HTML table size.

finding.remediation: Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/total column counts before generating any table markup; charge all generated WML to an expansion budget and return a typed input-limit refusal.

counterEvidence: ZIP and XML budgets limit original package entries; they do not limit the numeric colspan or derived WML.
Page raster MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is reached later and does not constrain this importer.
limitations: No runtime reproduction or exact memory measurement; numeric allocation consequence follows directly from the loop.
validation.summary: Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes → with_layout admission → altChunk relationship load → HTML td colspan → cell span → end_table cols → per-column String growth.

impact.why: Loss of embedding process/instance availability.

likelihood.why: A small numeric HTML field directly determines work.

remediationTests: Unit tests with a small configured column cap cover the inclusive limit, one above it, oversized numeric values, and sums of several otherwise valid spans.

rootCause.summary: The nesting guard tracks recursive parser calls. nested_list instead iteratively takes its previous output node as a new script base, preserving existing Scripts nodes through take_base. Each one-character script argument finishes before the next wrapper is added, so parse depth remains shallow while AST depth grows with input length. Writer::node recurses into that unbounded base through argument/nodes; no AST-depth or iterative traversal/destruction control intervenes.

findings.remediation: Bound actual AST depth and work when wrapping previous script/prime bases, and use iterative writing and safe nonrecursive destruction so rejection cannot itself drop an attacker-deep tree recursively.

counterEvidence: The 64-level parser guard protects recursively nested groups/commands, not this iterative AST wrapping.
No runtime threshold or crafted input was measured; exact stack/trap behavior is platform-dependent.
limitations: No application code, tests, exploit input or network activity executed.
validation.summary: Parent verified the 64 parser-call limit, one-character argument consumption, iterative wrapping, preservation of prior Scripts nodes, nonrecursive merge behavior, and unguarded writer recursion. A flat a^1^1... expression can therefore create arbitrary AST depth without violating the guarded syntax depth. markdown_to_docx assembles math by calling math::omml, which directly serializes equation(latex).

rootCause.summary: The nesting guard tracks recursive parser calls. nested_list instead iteratively takes its previous output node as a new script base, preserving existing Scripts nodes through take_base. Writer::node recurses into that unbounded base through argument/nodes; no AST-depth or iterative traversal/destruction control intervenes.

finding.remediation: Bound actual AST depth and work when wrapping previous script/prime bases, and use iterative writing and safe nonrecursive destruction so rejection cannot itself drop an attacker-deep tree recursively.

findings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
findings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets.

severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.
severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.

confidence.rationale: Independent worker and parent verified the concrete input-to-sink control failure statically; exact runtime resource/failure thresholds were not measured.

rootCause.summary: raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.

findings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.

rootCause.summary:

The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.

returnedFinding.title: Markdown reference documents reach recursive XML parsing without depth admission
returnedFinding.body: A caller-supplied reference DOCX is opened with PartFs::open and its main XML is passed into frame/final_section without package admission or checked XML parsing. PartFs bounds ZIP sizes and entry counts but does not enforce XML depth on document parts. final_section calls the explicitly unchecked Dom::parse_xdocument, whose parse_element recursively descends for every nested element without a depth limit. Consequently, a deeply nested reference document can exhaust the native Python/Rust process stack or trap the WASM instance despite the advertised max_xml_depth=256 policy. This is reachable through Rust markdown_to_docx, Python from_markdown(reference=...), WASM markdownToDocx(..., reference), and CLI --reference-doc conversion paths.
returnedFinding.attackerControl: Reference DOCX bytes supplied to an application or conversion workflow accepting untrusted templates.
returnedFinding.protectedAsset: Availability of the embedding Python/Rust process, conversion worker or WASM instance.
prerequisites: The application accepts an attacker-supplied reference document rather than selecting exclusively trusted templates.
The application does not independently admit/check the reference before conversion.

jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1204-1218 constructs options and directly calls shared markdown_to_docx.
jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:1438-1449 and 1482-1488 expose the equivalent reference-byte path.
src/markdown/write.rs:59-108 reaches package::assemble without admitting the reference.
src/markdown/package.rs:108-126 opens the reference and calls frame; 545-548 parses its complete main XML with Dom::parse_xdocument.

src/opc/mod.rs:282-351 enforces byte/entry/inflation limits and checks OPC metadata attributes, but performs no depth validation on ordinary document XML; 512-524 connects PartFs::open to that reader.
src/xmllinq/parse.rs:90-108 explicitly identifies the parser as unchecked; 555-626 has no depth guard and 660-662 recursively invokes parse_element.
Native CLI reference loading at src/bin/jubarte.rs:3367-3371 uses read_document; 2740-2756 only invokes refused_input, which is sniff/sniff_package at src/cli.rs:1992-1997.
Python CLI reference loading at jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:665 uses _read; 61-69 only invokes refused_input before returning bytes.
npm CLI reference loading at jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:242-252 feeds the same conversion path.
counterevidenceAndLimits: ZIP compressed-size, entry-count and inflation budgets still apply through PartFs::open; this finding concerns the missing XML-depth gate.
Normal inspection/edit paths perform admission before parsing and are not implicated by this reference-specific trace.
No public deployment, authenticated tenant boundary or universal remote reachability is assumed.
No triggering input was created and no application code was executed; stack threshold and precise platform failure behavior were not measured.
returnedFinding.remediation: Admit the caller-supplied reference with the selected InputLimits before any reference XML reaches unchecked DOM parsing, including the main document and preserved auxiliary parts. Alternatively, make each reference consumer use checked parsing with the same explicit limits; preserve malformed-document errors rather than silently weakening policy.

findings.title: Large page coordinates make border rendering loop without progress
findings.summary: Finite page dimensions and margins from DOCX can place a dotted border at coordinates where its f32 increment rounds to zero. Rendering then loops indefinitely while appending drawing operations, exhausting memory.

severity.rationale: Ordinary document rendering crosses from supplier-controlled section geometry to a nonterminating loop; availability is affected without host configuration. CPU/memory limits contain the worker but still permit denial of service.
severity.changeConditions: Reject excessive geometry, compute bounded integer segment counts and enforce operation budgets; isolation reduces shared-host consequences.

confidence.rationale: Parent confirmed unbounded geometry, text-relative endpoints, f32 step and per-iteration push. At1e9 float spacing exceeds1, proving nonprogress. No runtime hang executed.

taxonomy.category: Nonprogressing floating-point rendering loop

codeEvidence.label: Page and margins accept unbounded lengths
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker page width and left margin become f32 coordinates without a maximum.

codeEvidence.label: Border widths and style determine the step
codeEvidence.explanation: sz=1 maps to 0.24pt; dotted style later clamps on/off to0.5 each.

codeEvidence.label: Text-relative border uses large margins
codeEvidence.explanation: Default text-relative border places left endpoint at the unbounded margin.

codeEvidence.label: Float loop lacks progress and operation budget
codeEvidence.explanation: At p=1e9, f32 p+1 equals p; condition remains true and each iteration adds an operation.

codeEvidence.label: Each iteration appends a drawing operation
codeEvidence.explanation: Even zero-length coordinate progress pushes a minimum-width FillRect, exhausting memory.

rootCause.summary: `apply_sect_pr()` accepts unbounded f32 page dimensions and margins. A text-relative border starts at that margin. Dotted-border painting clamps on/off intervals to0.5 each, then repeatedly adds1 to the f32 position. At a large finite coordinate this addition cannot change the value; the while condition remains true and each iteration pushes another FillRect.

findings.remediation: Validate finite, reasonable page/margin/border geometry before layout. Use a bounded integer segment count instead of open-ended float accumulation, enforce a maximum border-operation budget, and explicitly refuse any step that cannot advance.

counterEvidence: All trigger numbers are finite; a NaN/infinity-only check would not fix the problem.
word_pgsz_pt only adjusts two A4 sizes and otherwise returns the supplied size.
MAX_PAGE_PIXELS applies after this layout loop, and PDF/render reports reach it too.
Process limits can kill the worker, not make the loop terminate.
limitations: No product execution, hang or allocation-failure reproduction performed.
validation.method: Independent parent static source and arithmetic review
validation.summary: pgSz width40000000000twips gives2e9pt; pgMar left20000000000 gives1e9pt. A top dotted border sz1 space0 starts at1e9 and ends near2e9. Its1pt total increment is smaller than the f32 representable spacing, so p never advances. Layout::new calls chrome/paint_pg_borders before PDF/PNG emission.

findings.title: Redaction succeeds while UTF-16 XML retains the removed text
findings.summary: The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing.

severity.rationale: An outgoing document can disclose text the user explicitly asked to remove. A supplier can place a duplicate in supported customXml and the user performs ordinary redaction; successful checking makes the confidentiality failure likely when that document is shared.
severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on sensitivity and subsequent sharing. Consistent BOM-aware decoding and fail-closed scanning remove the bypass.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified UTF16 admission, raw part retention/output, XML-only lossy UTF8 branch and success gate. Baseline validation allows unchanged auxiliary issues. No product execution was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Documented redaction confidentiality promise
codeEvidence.code:
Replace the unique occurrence of ``find`` (or its ``occurrence``-th hit) with one block per character.

The redaction is no tracked change: the clean copy and the redline
both show the blocks. The plan is refused with ``REDACTION_LEAK``
when the text still occurs anywhere in either document (another
paragraph, a comment, a header, the properties); the report never

codeEvidence.explanation: The promised REDACTION_LEAK refusal applies when target text remains anywhere in either output.

codeEvidence.label: XML fallback cannot reconstruct UTF-16
codeEvidence.explanation: The fallback searches the same lossy UTF-8 string, which retains interleaved NULs rather than the decoded target.

rootCause.summary: Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part.

findings.remediation: Decode every XML part with the same BOM-aware policy as admission before semantic leak scanning. Fail closed on unsupported/undecodable representations and retain raw UTF8 and both UTF16 byte-order checks as defense in depth. Use the same decoding across leak checks and package validation.

counterEvidence: Unreadable archives/entries and inflation-budget failures correctly refuse redaction.
UTF8 XML entities and Word text split across runs are handled.
UTF16 raw matching exists for non-XML parts only.
Normal redaction outcome diagnostics avoid repeating the secret.
Archive read/inflation failures fail closed and UTF-8 XML comments, processing instructions/entities and joined Word runs are scanned.
Neither those controls nor the non-XML UTF-16LE fallback covers UTF-16 XML.
A simple transitional package does not need strict translation that could rewrite auxiliary XML.
limitations: No product-generated trigger or runtime redaction test executed.
Disclosure requires the resulting package to be shared or inspected by another party.
Static source validation only; disclosure additionally requires sharing the returned document with a recipient.

Both final artifacts are checked with that same routine. Existing malformed-XML validation findings are baseline, not automatically introduced failures.
Additional validated trace follows public edit preparation into both serialized artifacts, unchanged auxiliary bytes and xml_holds fallback. Ordinary Transitional main XML avoids normalization rewriting the auxiliary UTF-16 copy. Both LE/BE supported encodings and the standalone leaks API share the missing XML decoding control.

rootCause.summary: Admission decodes BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE XML for validation, so a `customXml/item1.xml` holding the target text is supported input. rootCause.summary:
`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization.
Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions.

findings.remediation: Resolve all core, extended and custom property parts through authoritative package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target according to docprops selection, and remove corresponding custom-property parts/relationships/content-type records coherently. Verify the selected privacy postcondition; refuse unsupported or ambiguous layouts rather than returning a successfully scrubbed copy. Preserve intentional title/subject/application and revision-date retention. Missing/invalid selected targets require explicit refusal or documented safe handling; default public and CLI callers must enforce the same postcondition.

findings.title: Opaque DTD and top-level CDATA bypass package XML depth checks
findings.summary: Package admission ignores opaque DTD and top-level CDATA events, while the permissive DOM handles top-level <! constructs by skipping only to the first '>'. A delimiter within a quoted entity or CDATA body exposes deeply nested literal markup as recursive elements, bypassing admission depth and potentially exhausting the host stack. Rendering and lazy WmlDocument main-part access are preserved affected entrypoints.

severity.rationale: A small ordinary-named document part can cause process stack exhaustion through public document processing. Impact is availability without privileged configuration; no external entity fetch or code execution is asserted.
severity.changeConditions: Rejecting DTD declarations at package admission and enforcing parser depth makes the representations agree. Isolated workers reduce shared-host impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent parent traced both parser interpretations and checked the locked quick-xml0.42 DTD parser's quote-sensitive skip. No runtime stack exhaustion was executed; the exact crash depth depends on runtime stack size.
